newsitem.title: UK: IGC sees lower Morocco cereals crop, more imports.
newsitem.headline: IGC sees lower Morocco cereals crop, more imports.

text.p: Cereals production in Morocco is expected to be sharply lower in 1997 in both the wheat and coarse grains sectors, the International Grains Council (IGC) said on Thursday.

The IGC slashed its forecasts for both sectors from the figures it issued on May, lowering wheat by 1.7 million tonnes to 2.0 million and coarse grains by 1.2 million to 1.8 million. the IGC estimated 1996 output at 5.9 million tonnes for wheat and 4.1 million tonnes forcoarse grains.
Morocco's wheat imports were now expected to rise to 2.2 million tonnes in 1997/98, compared with the previous forecast of 1.6 million and 1.4 million in 1996/97.
On Wednesday, Morocco's Agriculture Minister said the cereals harvest was expected to fall by two-thirds in 1996/97 due to bad weather conditions.
He cited heavy rains earlier this year and drought which then hit some agricultural areas, causing a sharp fall in agriculture output, mainly in the cereals sector.
